messages:
alex: Heads up - saw a throughput dip on the 8xA100 perf job when LL128 + 4 NCCL channels + KV-prefetch is enabled. Baseline (LL128, 2 channels, prefetch off) was stable ~320 tokens/s, current config dropped to ~230 and variance spiked. Traces attached.

maria: Ugh. Any obvious allreduce hotspots in the nsys capture?

alex: Quick grep from the trace shows long gaps on each step around allreduce start/finish. Paste:

```
# simplified timeline summary (ns)
step 123: compute 1.1ms -> allreduce 5.2ms -> stall 0.9ms
step 124: compute 1.0ms -> allreduce 1.3ms -> stall 0.8ms
step 125: compute 1.2ms -> allreduce 6.0ms -> stall 1.1ms
# correlated with KV-cache miss bursts
```

alex: Note: when KV miss ratio > 30% we see those 5-6ms spikes. With prefetch off, allreduce stays ~1.2ms steady.

jordan: Interesting. Could be inter-play between prefetch network bursts and NCCL channels causing congestion/serialized collectives. Did you try lowering channels?

alex: Not yet for that job. We ran channels=4 because LL128 seemed to need more parallelism for seq len > 2048.

kai: Two hypotheses: 1) prefetch bursts saturate NIC at certain windows -> algorithm/proto fallback causes slow path, 2) kernel selector fragmentation increases compute variance leading to worse overlap. We should isolate NIC saturation vs NCCL algo regression.

maria: Can you run a quick sweep: channels=2 vs 4, prefetch on/off, and force LL vs LL128? Keep other params same. Small batch of 50 steps is fine.

alex: Scheduling sweep queued. Job name: ll128-prefetch-sweep-184250. Will log nsys and nccl topo.

devops-bot: Job queued: job/ll128-prefetch-sweep-184250 (8xA100, 4xslot). Started.

jordan: If you can, also capture NCCL debug env: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ALGO=RING,NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE and a run forcing TREE+LL algorithm for comparison. Sometimes LL128 with proto=LL causes fallback to a slower path when NIC buffers are congested.

alex: Good call. I'll include env toggles: NCCL_ALGO=RING/TREE/LL, NCCL_PROTO=LL/LL128/SIMPLE. And set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0/1 to test RDMA vs SHM.

kai: Also instrument per-GPU timeline for memcpy(GB) from KV prefetch. If prefetch injects big P2P writes at the same time as allreduce, we'll see contention.

alex: Quick interim result from channels=2, prefetch=on, algo=LL, proto=LL128: throughput recovered to ~305 tokens/s and allreduce steady ~1.25ms. channels=4, same settings -> regression to ~235. So channels=4 is correlated.

maria: So 4 channels + prefetch on seems to expose a corner where NCCL channel scheduling interacts poorly with our prefetch traffic. Possible contention on NIC queue pairs?

jordan: That matches my reading. With more channels NCCL uses more hardware QPs and may saturate CQE handling. Combined with prefetch bursts we might hit head-of-line issues.

alex: Action items:
- alex: run a micro-sweep setting NIC pacing + per-channel throttling (NCCL_NET_GDR_READ/WRITE tuning) and collect per-QP packet drops.
- jordan: add a lightweight kernel selector metric to trace to detect when compute switches between quantized kernel variants mid-run.
- kai: prototype a prefetch smoothing gate (leaky-bucket) to limit burst amplitude.

maria: Adding: try disabling continuous batching during prefetch windows to reduce simultaneous allreduce starts (maybe stagger KV pulls).

devops-bot: Job complete: job/ll128-prefetch-sweep-184250. Artifacts: s3://redwood-experiments/ll128-prefetch-sweep-184250/nsys.zip, nccl.logs.

alex: I'll post the perf diffs and a small reproducer script after the next sweep. Thanks all :thumbsup:
